title: The Final Countdown
source_notes: Pitches, exact sixteenth/eighth-note rhythm and ties visually checked against the piano melody on printed pages 1-4 of arranger Pierre Loiselle's self-published score. Uses its bars 1-8, then 13-16, with an added F# minor cadence. Lead uses original-key pitches C#5/B4/F#4/D5 etc. Tied notes are merged. The initial 1.5 beats of rest are omitted so the recognisable C#5-B4-C#5 fanfare starts instantly. Tempo 118 BPM and octave choices are arrangement decisions; this is an independently sequenced fart arrangement, not original-recording audio. Harmonic extensions are optional accompaniment colour. For version 5.0 the complete melody and all harmonies are transposed down five semitones from the accepted F# minor score into C# minor. Rhythm, note durations and tempo are unchanged.
musical_direction: Arena-rock fart fanfare in a lower C# minor register. Keep the accepted melody, phrasing, bass gallop and orchestration, transposing every pitched voice down five semitones.

title: The Imperial March
source_notes: Melody and note durations visually checked against the official Faber/Warner-Chappell piano sample, printed page 28, bars 5-16 (the 4-bar introduction is omitted). The publisher sample is marked approximately 100 BPM; 108 BPM is the creative arrangement tempo. All melody pitches are transposed down one octave from that piano notation. The defining figures use dotted eighth + sixteenth (0.75 + 0.25 quarter-note beats), not straight eighths or triplets. F# and Eb in the upper chromatic descent are enharmonic spellings of the printed F# and D#. Chord events below are simplified arrangement guidance, not a transcription of the original orchestration.
musical_direction: A grand, silly fart brass band, 26.67 seconds before the release tail. Start the recognizable lead at beat 0 without an intro. Opening register G3, climactic high G4. Keep melody pitches exact; make rests and the dotted-eighth/sixteenth snaps crisp, with note gates around 75-85% except the final half-note. Alternate several pitched short dry rasps and resonant brass-like farts across melodic notes without changing the fundamental. Layer a quieter octave-down bass fart on strong beats, sparse triad stabs (two or three different timbres) under the first three repeated notes, and airy little puffs as snare on beats 1 and 3 of each bar. Add restrained marching 16th puffs in the written rests at beats 15, 21.0-21.5, 25.0-25.5, 37.0-37.5 and 41.0-41.5; avoid masking the Eb/Bb lead snaps. Give bars 9-12 a larger supporting ensemble and a small fill into beat 44. Finish with the G minor cadence and one low, rounded fart release. Lower harmonies are a pad/stab layer, never a competing tune.
